regimens.indication: Edema Associated with Congestive Heart Failure, Cirrhosis of the Liver, and Renal Disease Including Nephrotic Syndrome (Adults)

refs.quote: LASIX is indicated in adults and pediatric patients for the treatment of edema associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and renal disease, including the nephrotic syndrome.

Adults -- The usual initial dose of LASIX is 20 mg to 80mg given as a single dose. Ordinarily a prompt diuresis ensues. If needed, the same dose can be administered 6 to 8 hours later or the dose may be increased.

dose.frequency: single initial dose, then once or twice daily

regimens.dose_text: Usual initial dose: 20 to 80 mg orally as a single dose; may repeat same dose or increase by 20-40 mg not sooner than 6-8 hours later until desired diuresis, then give once or twice daily (e.g., 8 am and 2 pm). May carefully titrate up to 600 mg/day in clinically severe edematous states.

regimens.indication: Edema Associated with Congestive Heart Failure, Cirrhosis, and Renal Disease (Pediatric Patients)

refs.quote: Pediatric patients -- The usual initial dose of oral LASIX in pediatric patients is 2 mg/kg body weight, given as a single dose. If the diuretic response is not satisfactory after the initial dose, dosage may be increased by 1 or 2 mg/kg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours after the previous dose. Doses greater than 6 mg/kg body weight are not recommended.

dose.frequency: single initial dose, adjust to minimum effective maintenance

regimens.dose_text: Usual initial oral dose: 2 mg/kg body weight as a single dose; may increase by 1 or 2 mg/kg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours later if diuresis unsatisfactory. Doses > 6 mg/kg body weight are not recommended.

refs.quote: Adults -- The usual initial dose of LASIX for hypertension is 80mg, usually divided into 40mg twice a day. Dosage should then be adjusted according to response.

regimens.dose_text: Usual initial dose: 80 mg daily, usually divided into 40 mg orally twice daily; adjust according to response. Reduce dosage of other antihypertensive agents by at least 50% when adding LASIX.

renal_impairment.description: Contraindicated in patients with anuria. Furosemide is substantially excreted by the kidney and risk of toxic reactions may be greater in impaired renal function; hemodialysis does not accelerate elimination.

This drug is known to be substantially excreted by the kidney, and the risk of toxic reactions to this drug may be greater in patients with impaired renal function.

mechanism_of_action.value: Furosemide is a loop diuretic that inhibits primarily the absorption of sodium and chloride in the proximal and distal tubules as well as the loop of Henle, independent of carbonic anhydrase or aldosterone inhibition.

refs.quote: It has been demonstrated that LASIX inhibits primarily the absorption of sodium and chloride not only in the proximal and distal tubu but also in the loop of Henle. The high degree of efficacy is largely due to the unique site of action.
Recent evidence suggests that furosemide glucuronide is the only or at least the major biotransformation product of furosemide in man.

value.effect: Phenytoin interferes directly with renal action of LASIX and decreases intestinal absorption, lowering peak serum furosemide concentrations.
value.management: Monitor diuretic response and adjust furosemide dose if needed.

refs.quote: Phenytoin interferes directly with renal action of LASIX. There is evidence that treatment with phenytoin leads to decreased intestinal absorption of LASIX, and consequently to lower peak serum furosemide concentrations.

value.effect: Simultaneous administration reduces natriuretic and antihypertensive effects of LASIX.
value.management: Separate intake of LASIX and sucralfate by at least two hours.

refs.quote: Simultaneous administration of sucralfate and LASIX tablets may reduce the natriuretic and antihypertensive effects of LASIX. Patients receiving both drugs should be observed closely to determine if the desired diuretic and/or antihypertensive effect of LASIX is achieved. The intake of LASIX and sucralfate should be separated by at least two hours.

value.effect: NSAIDs may reduce natriuretic/antihypertensive effects and increase BUN, creatinine, and potassium; high-dose salicylates may cause salicylate toxicity due to competitive renal excretion.
value.management: Observe patients closely for desired diuretic/antihypertensive effect and monitor renal function and electrolytes.
